beats.text: Think we're wilder than our parents? We're having less sex.
A national survey has asked Americans about their sex lives since nineteen eighty-nine. Over twenty-six thousand people.
By the early twenty-tens, adults had sex about nine times less per year than in the late nineties.
For married couples, the drop was even bigger. Sixteen times less a year.
One reason researchers point to: fewer young people have a steady partner.
So we might talk about sex more. But we're having less of it.

sources: Twenge, Sherman & Wells (2017). Declines in sexual frequency among American adults, 1989-2014. Archives of Sexual Behavior 46(8). GSS, N > 26,000; ~9 fewer times/year in 2010-2014 vs 1995-1999; married/cohabiting ~16 fewer times/year vs 2000-2004; fewer steady partners among younger cohorts. Via Phys.org 2017.
